video_title: Chris Finch: “We Did Anthony Edwards A DISSERVICE” + Why LaMelo Changes Everything

quotes.speaker: Chris Finch
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Finch admits Anthony Edwards was miscast as point guard
quotes.excerpt: We probably did Anthony a disservice last year at times playing him as a point guard.
quotes.quote: We probably did Anthony a disservice last year at times playing him as a point guard. Obviously, LaMelo is a phenomenal talent all by himself, but we needed the connective tissue. We needed the point guard play.

quotes.speaker: Chris Finch
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Finch on the lifestyle commitment required for NBA coaching
quotes.excerpt: It is a little bit of a lifestyle commitment. There is no doubt about it.
quotes.quote: It is a little bit of a lifestyle commitment. There is no doubt about it. I have been fortunate enough to coach a lot of guys, a lot of really good players. When you have a guy like Mike Conley who tells you, 'I never want to coach these guys,' you think to yourself, 'Maybe I picked the wrong profession.'

quotes.speaker: Chris Finch
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Finch explains the lack of playoffs in the English league
quotes.excerpt: The league in England is very much like the Premier League. There is no playoffs.
quotes.quote: The league in England is very much like the Premier League. There is no playoffs. Whoever finishes on top after the regular season is the regular season champion. The league just happened to come down to a winner-take-all game at his place, and we won it.

quotes.speaker: Chris Finch
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Finch on the need for high emotional intelligence in coaching
quotes.excerpt: To be in coaching these days, you have to have a high emotional intelligence.
quotes.quote: To be in coaching these days, you have to have a high emotional intelligence. You have to be able to vibe with your players and figure out what they need. On our team, I have been there since the beginning with Anthony Edwards. It is an evolution of how we coach him, how we approach him, and how we have to continue to hold him accountable, but that has to continue to change too.

quotes.speaker: Chris Finch
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Finch on the challenges of coaching in the G League
quotes.excerpt: I thought this coaching thing in the G League was going to be kind of easy.
quotes.quote: I thought this coaching thing in the G League was going to be kind of easy, and I realized this is not what I signed up for. I had to have a talk with myself and thought, 'I don't control who comes to my team. I can't control some of the personality dynamics. I just got to figure out how to navigate this.' It was a watershed moment for me because overseas, I would control who came to the team or who left.

quotes.speaker: Chris Finch
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Finch on the Timberwolves' roster improvements
quotes.excerpt: It is about making your best players better.
quotes.quote: It is about making your best players better. We probably did Anthony a disservice last year at times playing him as a point guard. It caught up to us, and he did a really great job, but in the playoffs, it was just double team after double team. We have to get him back to his natural position off the ball. We did not create enough catch-and-shoot threes for him. When you look at the numbers with LaMelo on the floor with his teammates, the efficiency and the production, Anthony Edwards shot 7% higher from the three-point line with LaMelo on the floor than he did without. That is a massive stat for a great shooter. We have never been able to unlock Rudy Gobert as a lob threat. We have not had that type of passer with the ball in his hands that much. We feel Jaden McDaniels is on the launchpad for another step forward. We have young guys ready to play, whether it be Terrence Shannon, Jaylen Clark, or Yohan Traore. These guys have earned consistent roles, and we had to create pathways for that. In one move, we felt we did all of this.

quotes.speaker: Chris Finch
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Finch on the importance of having the right veterans
quotes.excerpt: You have to have the right veterans. Not all veterans are great veterans.
quotes.quote: You have to have the right veterans. Not all veterans are great veterans. I was talking to DeAndre Jordan the other day. I commended him and said, 'What you are doing is incredible because you are bringing positivity, you are there, and you are ready to play if need be, and you have accepted your role.' I have actually talked to guys who have gotten to the twilight of their career and tried to encourage them to start thinking more along the line of being that type of veteran. But it is the competitiveness that they still have that they want to play, they want to play, they want to play. I think some front offices see that as maybe a little bit of an internal threat.

quotes.speaker: Chris Finch
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Finch on the Timberwolves' 'bad win' regular season
quotes.excerpt: The whole season kind of felt like a bad win.
quotes.quote: The whole season kind of felt like a bad win. We had high expectations and we had a lot of success getting to the Western Conference Finals, and we know that we have a long way to go still. At times we felt bored with the regular season. We were not playing our best basketball, but it all started to come together, and we played really well. I felt we would wake up in the playoffs. I was just praying we didn't get stuck in the play-in and kind of come out and have a shitty game and then lose it.

quotes.speaker: Chris Finch
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Finch on the team's depth and defensive creativity
quotes.excerpt: We are definitely going to have to be creative defensively, giving up size.
quotes.quote: We are definitely going to have to be creative defensively, giving up size. We went from probably having the best 48 minutes of depth at the four position across the league to, you know, kind of having a little bit more of a hole we got to figure out. But this goes back to, this is our third big swing since I have been here with Tim Conley. We brought in Rudy, traded KAT, brought in those guys, and now this one. So, we will always shift around what our best players can do and our identity will change a little bit, but we are pretty excited about it.

quotes.speaker: Chris Finch
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Finch on the importance of Rudy Gobert as a floor raiser
quotes.excerpt: He is a floor raiser. When he is out there every single night, you are going to be at a certain level.
quotes.quote: He is a floor raiser. When he is out there every single night, you are going to be at a certain level and have a chance to win every night. Great pro. With Rudy, his successes, the things that are going on in the background at a high level all the time are not always noticed. His mistakes or his, it's are loud and so people can point to them and he's, you know, and he's, I think it's a crime, it's a shame how people will criticize Rudy and, and you know, it's something internally that our guys have rallied around. Our guys have rallied around Rudy in, because they understand how important he is to us.
